transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
I can’t think straight anymore or make simple decisions at work or school, and it’s starting to scare me. I just feel so overwhelmed and like I can't keep up with anything anymore.
Have you been experiencing excessive worry or fear about everyday things, such as your performance at work or school, for more than six months?

Yes, I definitely have. I lie awake for hours with my mind racing, obsessing over mistakes I made during the day and spiraling into thoughts that I'm a terrible nurse and a disappointment. This constant worry and stress about my performance at work and school has been going on for over a year now.
Have you been avoiding certain situations or tasks at work or school because of your worries or fears?

I haven't been avoiding going to work or class entirely, but I did withdraw from my study groups because I felt too overwhelmed to keep up. Instead of avoiding my tasks, I get so caught up in second-guessing myself that I feel frozen, which really delays things like writing simple nursing notes or finishing my quizzes.

Can you tell me more about what you mean by 'frozen' when you're trying to complete tasks, and is this feeling of being 'frozen' more related to the fear of making mistakes or the fear of the situation itself?

It is definitely more about the fear of making mistakes and constantly second-guessing myself, especially since I got written up for a charting error. My brain feels so foggy that simple tasks like writing a nursing note or picking a quiz answer make me overthink every detail. I just end up staring at the screen, terrified of messing up again and unable to make a move.

Have you experienced any traumatic event, such as a life-threatening situation or a significant loss, that you think might be contributing to your current feelings of overwhelm and fear of making mistakes?

No, I haven't experienced any traumatic events or significant losses. My feelings of overwhelm are really just tied to the ongoing stress of trying to handle my full-time work schedule at the clinic and my nursing classes.
Do you often feel restless, on edge, or have an inability to relax, especially when you're not actively engaged in a task or activity?
I don't really feel restless or on edge. Instead, I feel extremely slowed down, exhausted, and completely drained most of the time.
Have you noticed any changes in your interest or pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy, such as hobbies or spending time with friends and family?

Yes, I've completely lost interest in things I used to love, like my evening jogs and knitting. Now, on my days off, I just lie in bed scrolling on my phone and ignoring texts from my friends, and I feel nothing when I think about what used to make me happy.
Can you tell me more about when you lost interest in activities you used to enjoy, was it before or after your worries and fears about work and school started to escalate?

It definitely started after the stress from work and school began to build up. Once the staffing shortages at the clinic got bad and I fell behind in my classes, I felt too exhausted and overwhelmed to keep up with my hobbies. Eventually, I just stopped jogging and knitting altogether because I didn't have the energy or interest anymore.
Did your feelings of overwhelm, worry, and loss of interest in activities occur at the same time, or did one set of symptoms seem to trigger the others?

The feeling of being overwhelmed by my work and school definitely came first. The stress of juggling the clinic shifts and my nursing classes made me lose control of my routine, which then triggered me to stop doing things I used to enjoy, like jogging and knitting, because I was just too exhausted. Over the following year, everything else just snowballed from there.
Have you been experiencing feelings of sadness, emptiness, or hopelessness most of the day, nearly every day, over the past two weeks?

Yes, most days I feel this heavy, gray cloud sitting on my chest, leaving me feeling sad and hopeless for no clear reason, and I just can't shake it off. This has been going on for way longer than two weeks—it's actually been about a year now, ever since I started working full-time at the clinic while beginning my classes.

Can you clarify if your feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and loss of interest in activities started immediately after your work and school stresses began, or if they developed over time as your stress and anxiety continued?

They definitely developed gradually over time rather than starting right away. At first, I was just trying to survive the overwhelming schedule and staffing shortages, but as the weeks of back-to-back shifts and coursework piled up, I slowly lost my routines and withdrew from things. That is when the heavy sadness and loss of interest really took over.
Do you think your feelings of sadness and hopelessness are more a result of your worries and fears about work and school, or do you feel they are a separate issue that you're dealing with?

While the intense stress of juggling work and school definitely triggered this and makes it worse, the sadness and hopelessness now feel like a heavy, gray cloud that is constantly there, even when nothing specific is going wrong. It really feels like its own separate, overwhelming issue that I just can't seem to shake off anymore.

Do you feel like your sadness and hopelessness are directly tied to your worries about work and school, or are they more of a constant, underlying feeling that you experience regardless of your specific worries?

Although work and school are incredibly stressful, the sadness feels more like a constant, underlying presence. It is like a heavy, gray cloud that sits on my chest even when nothing particularly bad is happening, leaving me feeling sad and hopeless for no clear reason.

Can you clarify if there was a specific period where your anxiety symptoms, such as excessive worry and fear of making mistakes, significantly improved, but your depressive symptoms, like sadness and loss of interest, persisted?
I'm not really sure about that. I haven't noticed a time when the worry and fear improved while the sadness stayed behind. It all just feels like it has been happening together constantly.

Can you think of any period in the past year when you felt significantly less anxious or worried about work and school, but still experienced feelings of sadness, hopelessness, or loss of interest in activities?

I can't really think of a period like that. The worry and anxiety about school and work have felt pretty constant over the past year, and even on my days off when I'm not physically there, the heavy sadness and the stress still seem completely tangled together.

Can you try to recall if there was ever a time when you felt the sadness and hopelessness lift for a while, but the worries and fears about work and school remained, or if these feelings have always been intertwined for you?

These feelings have always been completely intertwined for me. Ever since I started juggling full-time clinic work and my nursing classes a little over a year ago, the sadness, hopelessness, and constant worry have felt tangled together. One just feeds into the other, and I've never had a real break where the sadness actually lifted.

Do you think your worries and fears about work and school are the primary issue, and the sadness and hopelessness are a result of those worries, or do you feel like the sadness and hopelessness are a separate issue that contributes to your worries and fears?

While the worries about school and work are huge, this deep sadness feels like a separate, heavy blanket that is constantly there even on my days off. It feels like a constant gray cloud that makes it even harder to cope with those daily stressors, rather than just being a reaction to them.

Can you think of any instance where your anxiety about work and school significantly decreased, but your feelings of sadness and hopelessness persisted, or have these symptoms always been present together?

No, these symptoms have pretty much always been present together ever since my struggles started a little over a year ago. Even on my days off when I am away from the immediate stress of the clinic and classes, that heavy, gray cloud of sadness and hopelessness doesn't go away. I still just lie in bed feeling completely empty.
Can you estimate how many days out of the past month you've felt more dominated by worries and fears about work and school, versus days where the sadness and hopelessness felt more overwhelming?

It is really difficult to separate the two or give you an exact number of days because they feel constantly tangled together almost every day. The worries about work and school and those heavy feelings of sadness and hopelessness just blend into each other. It feels like they are both always there at the same time, so I can't really say one dominates more than the other.
Can you describe a recent situation where you felt anxious or worried about something specific, like a work task or school assignment, and how that anxiety affected your mood and behavior afterwards?

Recently, I froze for ten minutes trying to write a simple nursing note, terrified of making another charting error and proving I'm a terrible nurse who doesn't deserve to be in school. That anxiety completely paralyzed me, and afterward, I lay in bed for hours with my mind racing about my failures. It got so bad that I caught myself wishing I just wouldn't wake up the next morning.
Can you think of any time in the past year when you felt significantly less anxious or worried, but the sadness and hopelessness persisted, or have these symptoms always been intertwined?

I'm not really sure, because those feelings have always felt pretty tangled together for me. Over the past year, the worry, sadness, and hopelessness have just been constant without any clear separation. It really feels like they are always there at the exact same time.

Can you think of any period where you felt like you were able to manage your worries and fears about work and school effectively, but still experienced significant sadness or hopelessness, or did the improvement in one area always seem to coincide with improvement in the other?

I can't really think of a time when things were split like that or when I experienced any real improvement. Ever since this started about a year ago, the worries, sadness, and feeling overwhelmed have all been bound together in a continuous downward spiral. There has never really been a period where I was managing one while still struggling with the other.

Looking back over the past year, do you feel like there was ever a clear point where your worries and fears about work and school started to improve, but your feelings of sadness and hopelessness remained, or did these symptoms always seem to change together?

I'm not really sure, and I haven't noticed any clear split like that. Over the past year, it feels like all of these feelings—the sadness, hopelessness, and the stress about work and school—have just steadily gotten worse together. It never really felt like one of them was improving while the other stayed behind.

Can you try to recall if there was ever a brief period, even just a few days, where you felt a significant reduction in your worries and fears about work and school, but the sadness and hopelessness remained, or vice versa?

I honestly can't recall any period like that, even for just a few days. The worries about school and work, along with the constant sadness and hopelessness, have felt completely tied together and haven't really lifted or separated since everything started.
You mentioned wishing you wouldn't wake up the next morning, can you tell me more about what you meant by that and if you've had any thoughts of harming yourself?

On my worst nights, when I'm looking at my unfinished assignments and thinking about how far behind I am, I catch myself wishing I just wouldn't wake up the next morning. It really scares me that those kinds of thoughts are starting to make sense to me, but I don't have any plans to actually hurt myself. It is just a passive feeling of wanting all of this pressure to finally stop.
Have you ever had any thoughts of harming yourself or wished you were dead, and if so, how often have you been having these thoughts recently?

Yes, I do have those thoughts on my worst nights, especially when I'm looking at my unfinished assignments and worrying about work. I catch myself wishing I wouldn't wake up the next morning, and it really scares me that those thoughts are starting to make sense to me. It's not every single day, but it happens whenever the pressure feels too overwhelming to handle.

Can you try to recall if there was ever a time when your symptoms of sadness and hopelessness significantly improved, but your worries and fears about work and school persisted, or have these symptoms always been present together without any clear separation?

No, these feelings have always been completely tied together. Ever since I started juggling the clinic job and my nursing classes about a year ago, the sadness, hopelessness, and constant worries have been present together without any period of separation or improvement in my mood.
Can you estimate how many days in the past month you've felt more dominated by sadness and hopelessness versus days dominated by worries and fears about work and school?

It is really hard to give you an exact number of days or separate the two. The feelings of sadness and the constant worries about work and school feel deeply tangled together almost every day. It just feels like they are both constantly there at the same time.

Can you think of any instance where you felt a significant improvement in your mood, such as a few days where you didn't feel sad or hopeless, but your worries and fears about work and school remained, or vice versa?

No, I haven't really experienced any periods of significant mood improvement or times when the sadness lifted while the worries remained. It has just felt like a constant, heavy gray cloud for the past year without any breaks.

Looking back, do you feel like your worries and fears about work and school were the initial problem that then led to feelings of sadness and hopelessness, or did the sadness and hopelessness start around the same time as your worries?

I'd say the sadness and hopelessness started around the same time as the overwhelming stress and worries. About a year ago, when I began juggling the full-time clinic shifts and my nursing classes, that heavy, gray cloud of sadness seemed to set in right alongside the mounting pressure of trying to keep up.
